memory_candidates.content: When a plan deletes a file from the agent-system source store and creates a NEW source-store test file in the same or an earlier phase, the new test file needs an explicit entry in manifest.json's provides.scripts array, separate from any suite-classification.data row. The manifest-driven deploy copier (loader.lua's M.copy_category) only deploys files listed in provides.scripts; a suite-classification.data row alone deploys fine via a different mechanism but does not cause the .sh file itself to be copied. Symptom: gate 5 (manifest category parity) reports 'Missing scripts: scripts/tests/<name>.sh' after a redeploy even though the file exists in the source store and passes standalone.

In this dev environment, a plain foreground Bash call (even with the Bash tool's own timeout parameter raised well above 120000ms) gets auto-backgrounded by the harness after approximately 180 seconds regardless of the parameter value. verify-deploy.sh's full gate battery (especially gate 8 / run-all.sh's ~200-suite run) routinely takes 500-1200+ seconds under concurrent multi-agent load. The reliable idiom is: launch with `nohup <cmd> > logfile 2>&1 & disown`, capture the PID via pgrep if `$!` is lost across tool calls, then poll with a `kill -0 "$pid"` loop inside repeated ~170s Bash calls (each call's own wait loop must stay under the ~180s auto-background threshold), reading the log file directly once the PID is confirmed dead. A killed/orphaned run can leave a stale specs/.gate-lock behind; release it with `bash .claude/scripts/task-lock.sh gate-release "<token-from-owner-file>"` (the deployed copy, not the source store) rather than rm -rf.
